name: CISSP dump (reviewed) - Domain 5: Identity and Access Management

questions.stem: An organization has doubled in size due to a rapid market share increase. The size of the Information Technology (IT) staff has maintained pace with this growth. The organization hires several contractors whose onsite time is limited. The IT department has pushed its limits building servers and rolling out workstations and has a backlog of account management requests. Which contract is BEST in offloading the task from the IT staff?
questions.explanation: The backlog is account management for transient contractors, which IDaaS addresses directly.
optionNotes: PaaS addresses development platforms, not accounts.
Correct: IDaaS offloads account management for transient contractors.
DaaS reduces workstation builds but not account backlog.
SaaS replaces applications, not identity administration.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an effective control in preventing electronic cloning of Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) based access cards?
options: Physical Access Control System (PACS) repeated attempt detection
questions.explanation: Asymmetric CAK challenge-response proves possession of a private key that cannot be copied from the card.
optionNotes: PIV is the card standard, not an anti-cloning mechanism itself.
CHUID is static and can be copied/replayed.
Repeated-attempt detection doesn't stop a perfect clone.
Correct: private key never leaves card, defeating cloning.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes an access control method utilizing cryptographic keys derived from a smart card private key that is embedded within mobile devices?
questions.explanation: A derived credential is a key placed on a mobile device derived from the user's PIV smart card credential.
optionNotes: Correct: NIST SP 800-157 derived PIV credential.
Temporary credentials are short-lived tokens (cloud).
Generic description, not the defined term.
HTTP digest uses hashed passwords.

questions.stem: A manufacturing organization wants to establish a Federated Identity Management (FIM) system with its 20 different supplier companies. Which of the following is the BEST solution for the manufacturing organization?
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said C] With many partner organizations, the hard problem in federation is establishing trust. If every pair of organizations cross-certifies, the number of trust relationships grows rapidly and becomes unmanageable at 20 suppliers. A trusted third party that each organization trusts gives one hub and scales well. SAML is the protocol that carries the assertions once trust exists. It is not the trust model itself.
optionNotes: Correct: each organization trusts one third party, so trust scales cleanly to 20 suppliers.
Wrong: LDAP is a directory access protocol and does not provide cross-organization federation.
Wrong: SAML carries assertions but does not by itself establish trust among 20 separate organizations.
Wrong: pairwise cross-certification grows to many trust links and is hard to manage with 20 partners.

questions.stem: What is the BEST approach for controlling access to highly sensitive information when employees have the same level of security clearance?
questions.explanation: With equal clearance, least privilege (need-to-know) restricts access to highly sensitive data.
optionNotes: Logs are detective.
Roles may still grant broad access.
Authentication strength doesn't limit access scope.
Correct: need-to-know limits access among equal clearances.

questions.stem: Which one of the following describes granularity?
options: Maximum number of entries available in an Access Control List (ACL)
Fineness to which a trusted system can authenticate users
Number of violations divided by the number of total accesses
Fineness to which an access control system can be adjusted
questions.explanation: Granularity is how finely access control can be adjusted. Granularity is a property of the access control mechanism, not of authentication (B). Finer granularity lets permissions be set at the file, record or field level.
optionNotes: ACL size is a capacity limit, not granularity.
Granularity concerns access control, not authentication.
That ratio is a violation rate metric.
Right: granularity is how finely access control can be tuned.

questions.stem: An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is generating alarms that a user account has over 100 failed login attempts per minute. A sniffer is placed on the network, and a variety of passwords for that user are noted. Which of the following is MOST likely occurring?
questions.explanation: Many password guesses against one account in rapid succession indicates a dictionary/brute-force attack. The sniffer shows many different passwords tried rapidly against one account, which points to a password-guessing (dictionary) attack. A DoS attack would aim at availability, not at guessing credentials.
optionNotes: Right: many different passwords tried rapidly against one account is a dictionary/password attack.
DoS aims at availability; varied passwords show credential guessing.
Spoofing fakes an identity/address, not guessing passwords.
A backdoor would not generate repeated failed logins.

questions.stem: Which security action should be taken FIRST when computer personnel are terminated from their jobs?
options: Require them to turn in their badge
Reduce their physical access level to the facility
questions.explanation: Logical access removal comes first upon termination to prevent damage. A badge (B) and physical access (D) matter too, but IT staff can do the most damage through logical access. Revoking that access first prevents sabotage and data theft.
optionNotes: Right: revoke logical access first to prevent sabotage or data theft.
Collecting the badge is important but after access removal.
Exit interviews are procedural and come later.
Physical access changes follow removal of system access.

questions.stem: A practice that permits the owner of a data object to grant other users access to that object would usually provide
questions.explanation: Owner-granted access is Discretionary Access Control. Under MAC (A) the system enforces labels and owners cannot grant access. Owner discretion to grant access is the defining feature of DAC; the other terms are not standard models.
optionNotes: MAC is set by labels/system, not owner.
Not a standard model term.
Not a standard model term.
Right: owner-granted access is DAC.

questions.stem: When designing a networked Information System (IS) where there will be several different types of individual access, what is the FIRST step that should be taken to ensure all access control requirements are addressed?
options: Develop a Role Based Access Control (RBAC) list.
questions.explanation: Before choosing a mechanism, designers should map every subject type to the objects and rights it needs. A user access matrix captures all those requirements; ACLs, roles and profiles are implemented from it.
optionNotes: Profiles are built after requirements are known
Right: captures all subject/object/rights requirements
ACLs are columns of the matrix, derived later
RBAC is an implementation choice made after requirements

questions.stem: Which of the following is an essential element of a privileged identity lifecycle management?
options: Regularly perform account re-validation and approval
Account provisioning based on multi-factor authentication
Frequently review performed activities and request justification
Account information to be provided by supervisor or line manager
questions.explanation: Privileged identities need periodic revalidation and reapproval so stale or excessive rights are removed. This recertification is a core lifecycle element.
optionNotes: Right: recertification keeps privileges justified
MFA is an authentication control, not lifecycle management
Activity review is monitoring, not identity lifecycle
Who supplies account data is a minor process detail

questions.stem: Which one of the following security mechanisms provides the BEST way to restrict the execution of privileged procedures?
questions.explanation: RBAC ties privileged procedures to specific roles, so only users in authorised roles can run them. That directly restricts execution.
optionNotes: Right: authorisation by role restricts privileged functions
Biometrics authenticate but do not define what one may run
Federation shares identities across domains
Hardening reduces attack surface but does not govern who runs procedures

questions.stem: Why must all users be positively identified prior to using multi-user computers?
options: To provide access to system privileges
To provide access to the operating system
To ensure that unauthorized persons cannot access the computers
To ensure that management knows what users are currently logged on
questions.explanation: Identification and authentication ensure that only authorised people use a shared system and allow actions to be attributed to individuals.
optionNotes: Privileges come from authorisation after identification
OS access is too narrow a description
Right: keeps out unauthorised persons
Knowing who is logged on is a side benefit

questions.stem: Logical access control programs are MOST effective when they are
options: made part of the operating system.
questions.explanation: Access controls built into the operating system are applied consistently and are hard to bypass. Add-on programs can be circumvented.
optionNotes: Auditor approval does not add effectiveness
Tokens strengthen authentication, not the access control program
Who maintains it does not determine effectiveness
Right: OS integration prevents bypass

questions.stem: Which of the following is an authentication protocol in which a new random number is generated uniquely for each login session?
questions.explanation: CHAP uses a fresh random challenge for each authentication, which the client hashes with the shared secret; this defeats replay.
optionNotes: A fresh random challenge per session is hashed with the shared secret, defeating replay
PPP is the link-layer framing protocol that carries CHAP/PAP, not itself the challenge scheme
EAP is a framework; any challenge depends on the chosen method
PAP sends the password in cleartext with no challenge

questions.stem: Why MUST a Kerberos server be well protected from unauthorized access?
options: It contains the keys of all clients.
It always operates at root privilege.
It contains all the tickets for services.
It contains the Internet Protocol (IP) address of all network entities.
questions.explanation: The KDC stores the secret keys of all principals; its compromise compromises the entire realm.
optionNotes: The KDC holds every principal's secret key, so compromise breaks the realm
Running as root is not the reason for protection
The KDC issues tickets but doesn't store them all
IP addresses are not sensitive Kerberos data

questions.stem: The type of authorized interactions a subject can have with an object is
questions.explanation: Permissions define the types of access (read, write, execute) a subject is authorized to have on an object.
optionNotes: Control is a broad safeguard term, not the access type
Permissions express allowed actions like read/write/execute
Procedures are documented steps
Protocols govern communications

questions.stem: The process of mutual authentication involves a computer system authenticating a user and authenticating the
options: user's access to all authorized objects.
computer system to the audit process.
questions.explanation: Mutual authentication means both the user and the system prove identity to each other.
optionNotes: Audit is not an authenticating party
The system proves its identity to the user too
That is authorization scope
Audit is not an authenticating party

questions.stem: The Structured Query Language (SQL) implements Discretionary Access Controls (DAC) using
questions.explanation: SQL grants and removes discretionary privileges with GRANT and REVOKE.
optionNotes: DML statements for rows, not privileges
GRANT gives and REVOKE removes privileges at owner's discretion
Not SQL privilege commands
ROLLBACK is transaction control; TERMINATE isn't DAC

questions.stem: Which one of the following is the MOST important in designing a biometric access system if it is essential that no one other than authorized individuals are admitted?
questions.explanation: To keep impostors out, minimize false acceptance (Type II errors).
optionNotes: Low FAR keeps unauthorized people out
FRR only inconveniences valid users
CER compares devices, not this goal
Not a standard biometric metric

questions.stem: A system is developed so that its business users can perform business functions but not user administration functions. Application administrators can perform administration functions but not user business functions. These capabilities are BEST described as
questions.explanation: Splitting business and administrative functions between different roles is separation of duties.
optionNotes: Least privilege is related but doesn't describe splitting duties
Rule-based control uses global rules, not role splits
MAC uses labels and clearances
Separating business and admin functions is separation of duties

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A new employee is given a laptop computer with full administrator access. This employee does not have a personal computer at home and has a child that uses the computer to send and receive e-mail, search the web, and use instant messaging. The organization's Information Technology (IT) department discovers that a peer-to-peer program has been installed on the computer using the employee's access. Which of the following could have MOST likely prevented the Peer-to-Peer (P2P) program from being installed on the computer?
options: Removing employee's full access to the computer
Supervising their child's use of the computer
Limiting computer's access to only the employee
Ensuring employee understands their business conduct guidelines
questions.explanation: The P2P program was installed using the employee's administrator rights. Applying least privilege by removing full admin access would have prevented installation regardless of who used the laptop.
optionNotes: Correct: without admin rights the software could not be installed.
Relies on the employee's supervision, not an enforceable control.
Does not stop the employee or malware from installing software with admin rights.
Awareness helps but is not a preventive technical control.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of two-factor authentication?
options: Retina scan and a palm print
Magnetic stripe card and an ID badge
Password and Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart (CAPTCHA)
questions.explanation: Two-factor authentication needs factors from different categories. A fingerprint (something you are) plus a smart card (something you have) qualifies; the others combine the same type or a non-authentication factor.
optionNotes: Both are biometrics: one factor type.
Correct: something you are plus something you have.
Both are possession items.
CAPTCHA proves humanity, not identity.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A large organization uses unique identifiers and requires them at the start of every system session. Application access is based on job classification. The organization is subject to periodic independent reviews of access controls and violations. The organization uses wired and wireless networks and remote access. The organization also uses secure connections to branch offices and secure backup and recovery strategies for selected information and processes. Which of the following BEST describes the access control methodology used?
questions.explanation: Application access is granted according to job classification, which is the defining characteristic of role-based access control. Least privilege is a principle, not a methodology.
optionNotes: A principle that RBAC can support, not the methodology.
Lattice models use security labels/levels, not job roles.
Correct: access by job classification is RBAC.
LDAP is a directory protocol, and the name is wrong.

questions.stem: Which of the following describes the concept of a Single Sign-On (SSO) system?
options: Users are authenticated to one system at a time.
Users are identified to multiple systems with several credentials.
Users are authenticated to multiple systems with one login.
Only one user is using the system at a time.
questions.explanation: Single sign-on lets users authenticate once and then access multiple systems without logging in again.
optionNotes: Opposite of SSO.
Multiple credentials is what SSO avoids.
Correct: one login gives access to many systems.
Describes single-user systems, unrelated.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST countermeasure to brute force login attacks?
options: Decreasing the number of concurrent user sessions
Restricting initial password delivery only in person
Introducing a delay after failed system access attempts
questions.explanation: Brute force relies on rapid repeated guesses. Introducing a delay or lockout after failed attempts makes such attacks impractical.
optionNotes: Does not limit guessing.
Concurrent sessions do not affect guess rate.
Protects initial password delivery, not guessing.
Correct: delays throttle guessing attempts.

questions.stem: What does secure authentication with logging provide?
questions.explanation: Authentication identifies the user and logging records actions, together establishing accountability for access.
optionNotes: Integrity needs hashing or similar controls.
Correct: identity plus logs gives accountability.
Not a meaningful security outcome.
SoD is an administrative design principle.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST mitigates a replay attack against a system using identity federation and Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) implementation?
options: Timed sessions and Secure Socket Layer (SSL)
Passwords with alpha-numeric and special characters
questions.explanation: Replay of SAML assertions is countered by limiting assertion/session validity in time and protecting them in transit with SSL/TLS so they cannot be captured and reused.
optionNotes: 2FA strengthens login but a captured assertion can still be replayed.
Certificates/tokens authenticate parties, not freshness of assertions.
Right: short validity windows plus TLS stop capture and reuse.
Password complexity is irrelevant to replaying assertions.

questions.stem: What physical characteristic does a retinal scan biometric device measure?
options: The amount of light reflected by the retina
The size, curvature, and shape of the retina
The pattern of blood vessels at the back of the eye
The pattern of light receptors at the back of the eye
questions.explanation: Retinal scans map the unique pattern of blood vessels on the retina at the back of the eye.
optionNotes: Reflected light is not the measured trait.
Retina size/shape is not what is matched.
Right: blood-vessel pattern on the retina is unique.
Light receptors are not the mapped feature.

questions.stem: What is a common challenge when implementing Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) for identity integration between on-premise environment and an external identity provider service?
options: Some users are not provisioned into the service.
SAML tokens are provided by the on-premise identity provider.
Single users cannot be revoked from the service.
questions.explanation: Federating with an external IdP commonly runs into provisioning gaps where some users are not provisioned into the service, since SAML handles authentication not provisioning.
optionNotes: Right: SAML doesn't provision accounts, so provisioning gaps are common.
Using the on-prem IdP is the normal design, not a challenge.
Revocation is possible by disabling the user at the IdP.
Assertions carrying user attributes is by design.

questions.stem: Which of the following violates identity and access management best practices?
questions.explanation: Generic/shared accounts break individual accountability and violate IAM best practice; the other account types are legitimate when managed.
optionNotes: Individual user accounts are best practice.
System/service accounts are acceptable when managed.
Right: shared generic accounts destroy accountability.
Privileged accounts are needed; they just need tight control.

questions.stem: What is the MOST effective method for gaining unauthorized access to a file protected with a long complex password?
questions.explanation: Long complex passwords resist brute force and dictionary attacks; social engineering bypasses password strength entirely by getting the user to reveal it.
optionNotes: Brute force is impractical against long complex passwords.
Frequency analysis targets classical ciphers, not passwords.
Right: tricking the holder bypasses password strength.
Dictionary attacks fail against complex non-word passwords.

questions.stem: What is the MOST important reason to configure unique user IDs?
questions.explanation: Unique IDs tie actions to individuals, which is the basis of accountability.
optionNotes: Right: unique IDs link actions to individuals.
Unique IDs don't reduce authentication errors.
Unique IDs don't stop password compromise.
SSO is a convenience, not the main reason for unique IDs.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A large organization uses unique identifiers and requires them at the start of every system session. Application access is based on job classification. The organization is subject to periodic independent reviews of access controls and violations. The organization uses wired and wireless networks and remote access. The organization also uses secure connections to branch offices and secure backup and recovery strategies for selected information and processes. What MUST the access control logs contain in addition to the identifier?
questions.explanation: For accountability and review, logs must record when access occurred along with who accessed.
optionNotes: Right: when access happened is essential for accountability.
Classification is metadata about the object, not a log requirement.
Denied attempts are useful but not the MUST.
Clearance is a user attribute, not something logs must hold.

questions.stem: Which of the following methods provides the MOST protection for user credentials?
questions.explanation: Digest authentication sends a hash of the credentials instead of cleartext, unlike Basic or plain forms-based authentication.
optionNotes: Forms auth often sends credentials in cleartext without TLS.
Right: digest sends a hashed challenge response.
Basic auth is only base64, effectively cleartext.
Self-registration is account creation, not protection.

questions.stem: Which of the following assures that rules are followed in an identity management architecture?
questions.explanation: The policy enforcement point carries out the PDP's decisions and so actually enforces the rules.
optionNotes: The database stores rules but enforces nothing.
Signatures give integrity/authenticity, not rule enforcement.
The PDP decides; it doesn't enforce.
Right: the PEP enforces the decision.

questions.stem: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) is necessary in many systems given common types of password attacks. Which of the following is a correct list of password attacks?
questions.explanation: Brute force, dictionary, phishing and keyloggers are all ways to obtain passwords.
optionNotes: Salami and polymorphism aren't password attacks.
Right: each is a way to get passwords.
These are malware names and nonsense.
These are controls, not attacks.

questions.stem: Which item below is a federated identity standard?
questions.explanation: SAML is the XML-based federated identity standard for exchanging authentication/authorization assertions across domains.
optionNotes: 802.11i is wireless security.
Kerberos is single-realm SSO, not a federation standard.
LDAP is a directory protocol.
Right: SAML is the federated assertion standard.

questions.stem: A large bank deploys hardware tokens to all customers that use their online banking system. The token generates and displays a six digit numeric password every 60 seconds. The customers must log into their bank accounts using this numeric password. This is an example of
questions.explanation: A token that generates a new code at fixed time intervals, synchronized with the server, is a synchronous (time-based) token.
optionNotes: Asynchronous tokens use challenge/event, not time.
It isn't SSO; it's for one bank system.
OTP alone is one factor, but the question is about the token type.
Right: time-synchronized token.

questions.stem: Refer to the information below to answer the question. A large organization uses unique identifiers and requires them at the start of every system session. Application access is based on job classification. The organization is subject to periodic independent reviews of access controls and violations. The organization uses wired and wireless networks and remote access. The organization also uses secure connections to branch offices and secure backup and recovery strategies for selected information and processes. In addition to authentication at the start of the user session, best practice would require re-authentication.
questions.explanation: Best practice is to require re-authentication after an idle timeout, so an unattended session cannot be misused. Other options are either impractical or meaningless.
optionNotes: Random periodic re-auth during active use burdens users without clear need
Per-process re-auth is impractical and not standard practice
Authenticating at sign-off serves no purpose
Inactivity timeout with re-auth protects unattended sessions

questions.stem: The BEST example of the concept of "something that a user has" when providing an authorized user access to a computing system is
options: a credential stored in a token.
questions.explanation: Possession factors are physical items such as tokens or smart cards. A credential stored in a token is something you have.
optionNotes: Hand geometry is a biometric (something you are)
A token holding a credential is a possession factor
A passphrase is something you know
A face is a biometric (something you are)

questions.stem: After a thorough analysis, it was discovered that a perpetrator compromised a network by gaining access to the network through a Secure Socket Layer (SSL) Virtual Private Network (VPN) gateway. The perpetrator guessed a username and brute forced the password to gain access. Which of the following BEST mitigates this issue?
options: Implement strong passwords authentication for VPN
Integrate the VPN with centralized credential stores
Implement an Internet Protocol Security (IPSec) client
questions.explanation: The attacker guessed a username and brute-forced the password; a second factor makes a cracked password insufficient. That directly mitigates the attack.
optionNotes: Stronger passwords slow brute force but don't stop it
Central credential stores don't stop guessing
IPsec changes the tunnel, not the authentication weakness
2FA defeats password-only compromise

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advantage of on premise Credential Management Systems?
questions.explanation: Running credential management on premises gives the organization full control over system configuration. It usually costs more and needs more administration.
optionNotes: Interoperability is not specifically improved on premises
On-premises gives direct control of configuration
Capital costs are higher on premises, not lower
Administrative overhead increases on premises

questions.stem: Which of the following information MUST be provided for user account provisioning?
questions.explanation: Each account needs a unique identifier to provide accountability. Other personal attributes are optional.
optionNotes: Full name is not mandatory and can be non-unique
A unique ID is essential for accountability
Security questions are optional recovery aids
DOB is unnecessary PII

questions.stem: Which technology is a prerequisite for populating the cloud-based directory in a federated identity solution?
questions.explanation: To populate a cloud directory for federation, identities are synchronized from the on-premises directory. Token and messaging tools do not provision directory entries.
optionNotes: Notification doesn't populate directories
Message queuing doesn't provide identity sync
Tokens assert authentication but don't populate directories
Directory synchronization populates the cloud directory

questions.stem: What is an important characteristic of Role Based Access Control (RBAC)?
options: Simplifies the management of access rights
questions.explanation: RBAC assigns permissions to roles and users to roles, which simplifies managing access rights as people join and move.
optionNotes: RBAC is non-discretionary, distinct from MAC
Role-based grouping simplifies rights management
Job rotation is not required by RBAC
RBAC does not mandate 2FA

questions.stem: A security professional is asked to provide a solution that restricts a bank teller to only perform a savings deposit transaction but allows a supervisor to perform corrections after the transaction. Which of the following is the MOST effective solution?
options: Access is determined by the system.
Access is based on user's role.
Access is based on data sensitivity.
questions.explanation: Teller and supervisor are job functions with different permitted transactions, which maps directly to role-based access control.
optionNotes: Rule-based applies global rules, not job functions
'System-determined' is vague
Role-based access matches teller vs supervisor
Sensitivity labels are MAC, not job function

questions.stem: During a fingerprint verification process, which of the following is used to verify identity and authentication?
options: A pressure value is compared with a stored template
Sets of digits are matched with stored values
A hash table is matched to a database of stored value
A template of minutiae is compared with a stored template
questions.explanation: Fingerprint systems extract minutiae such as ridge endings and bifurcations into a template, then compare it with the enrolled template.
optionNotes: Pressure is not the matched feature
Digits matching describes PINs
Hash tables aren't how fingerprint matching works
Minutiae templates are compared

questions.stem: A user sends an e-mail request asking for read-only access to files that are not considered sensitive. A Discretionary Access Control (DAC) methodology is in place. Which is the MOST suitable approach that the administrator should take?
options: Administrator should request data owner approval to the user access
Administrator should request manager approval for the user access
Administrator should directly grant the access to the non-sensitive files
Administrator should assess the user access need and either grant or deny the access
questions.explanation: Under DAC, the data owner decides who gets access. The administrator should obtain the owner's approval rather than decide alone, even for non-sensitive files.
optionNotes: Owner approval is how DAC grants access
Manager isn't the authority under DAC
Granting directly bypasses the owner
Admin isn't the decision maker

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BIGGEST weakness when using native Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) for authentication?
options: Authorizations are not included in the server response
Unsalted hashes are passed over the network
The authentication session can be replayed
Passwords are passed in clear text
questions.explanation: Native LDAP simple bind sends credentials in clear text unless protected by TLS/SASL.
optionNotes: Authorization is not the authentication weakness
Native LDAP simple bind sends no hashes, salted or not
Replay is possible but secondary to cleartext exposure
Simple bind transmits passwords in cleartext without TLS

questions.stem: Which of the following is generally indicative of a replay attack when dealing with biometric authentication?
options: False Acceptance Rate (FAR) is greater than 1 in 100,000
False Rejection Rate (FRR) is greater than 5 in 100
questions.explanation: Live biometric samples always vary slightly; an exact match with a stored template suggests a replayed captured sample.
optionNotes: A FAR threshold is a tuning metric, not a replay indicator
FRR measures false rejections, not replay
Poor templates cause errors, not replay evidence
Live samples always vary; an exact match signals a replayed capture

questions.stem: Discretionary Access Control (DAC) restricts access according to
questions.explanation: DAC grants access based on authorizations the owner gives to users/identities.
optionNotes: Classification labels are the basis of MAC
Page views are not an access control model basis
DAC uses owner-granted authorizations to identities
Accreditation is a system authorization decision, not DAC

questions.stem: In which identity management process is the subject's identity established?
questions.explanation: Enrollment (registration and identity proofing) establishes the subject's identity before credentials are issued.
optionNotes: Trust is not an identity lifecycle step that establishes identity
Provisioning creates accounts after identity is established
Authorization grants rights after authentication
Enrollment includes identity proofing that establishes identity

questions.stem: An employee of a retail company has been granted an extended leave of absence by Human Resources (HR). This information has been formally communicated to the access provisioning team. Which of the following is the BEST action to take?
options: Block user access and delete user account after six months.
Block access to the offices immediately.
questions.explanation: Temporarily disabling access during extended leave removes unused-access risk while allowing restoration on return.
optionNotes: Temporary revocation removes unneeded access, restorable on return
Deleting the account is excessive for an approved leave
Physical access alone leaves logical access open
Monitoring leaves unnecessary access active

questions.stem: If an identification process using a biometric system detects a 100% match between a presented template and a stored template, what is the interpretation of this result?
questions.explanation: Biometric samples never match perfectly; a 100% match suggests a replayed or tampered template.
optionNotes: User error lowers match quality, it does not yield 100%
Perfect match implies replayed or tampered template
Live samples never match exactly
A match is not an unsuccessful identification

questions.stem: For an organization considering two-factor authentication for secure network access, which of the following is MOST secure?
questions.explanation: Smart card (have) plus biometric (are) are two strong distinct factors.
optionNotes: Both may be 'something you have/know' and weaker
SSO is not an authentication factor
Tokens plus passphrase are fine but weaker than biometrics
Smart card plus biometric combine strong distinct factors

questions.stem: Discretionary Access Control (DAC) is based on which of the following?
questions.explanation: DAC lets the owner of an object decide which subjects may access it, so decisions rest on the identities of subjects and the objects they own. Labels belong to MAC, not DAC.
optionNotes: Source/destination describes network filtering, not DAC.
Right: owner grants access per subject identity and object.
Labels and clearances define MAC.
Standards and guidelines are governance documents, not an access model.

questions.stem: Which of the following could elicit a Denial of Service (DoS) attack against a credential management system?
options: Delayed revocation or destruction of credentials
questions.explanation: Tampering with the Certificate Revocation List can mark valid credentials as revoked, locking legitimate users out and denying service. The other options mostly allow continued unauthorized use rather than denial.
optionNotes: Delayed revocation enables misuse, not denial.
Right: falsely revoking certificates denies legitimate access.
Unauthorized renewal grants access rather than denying it.
Using decommissioned tokens is unauthorized access, not DoS.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML)?
questions.explanation: SAML carries authentication, attribute and authorization assertions that relying parties use to make and enforce access decisions. The other options are unrelated to SAML.
optionNotes: File system function.
Error-detection mechanism.
Certificate validation type, not SAML.
Right: assertions support authorization/policy enforcement.

questions.stem: What security risk does the role-based access approach mitigate MOST effectively?
options: Excessive access rights to systems and data
Segregation of duties conflicts within business applications
Lack of system administrator activity monitoring
questions.explanation: Roles grant only the permissions a job needs, avoiding ad hoc accumulation of rights. RBAC therefore most directly limits excessive access.
optionNotes: Right: roles constrain permissions to job need.
SoD conflicts need explicit constraints, not RBAC alone.
Monitoring is a separate control.
Request approval is a provisioning workflow issue.

questions.stem: Single Sign-On (SSO) is PRIMARILY designed to address which of the following?
questions.explanation: SSO ties a user's actions to one authenticated identity across systems, supporting accountability, and gives assurance in that identity. It is not mainly a confidentiality or availability control.
optionNotes: Not primary goals of SSO.
Availability is not addressed.
Not primary goals.
Right: single identity supports accountability and assurance.

questions.stem: Which of the following prevents improper aggregation of privileges in Role Based Access Control (RBAC)?
questions.explanation: Dynamic separation of duties stops a user from activating conflicting roles in the same session, preventing improper aggregation of privileges. Inheritance can actually aggregate rights.
optionNotes: Inheritance accumulates permissions.
Right: blocks conflicting role combinations.
An integrity model, not an RBAC feature.
Confidentiality model, not RBAC.

questions.stem: The implementation of which features of an identity management system reduces costs and administration overhead while improving audit and accountability?
questions.explanation: Self-service password resets and profile updates cut help-desk work and cost, and they log user actions for audit. The other features do not reduce administration in the same way.
optionNotes: 2FA adds cost and admin.
SSO reduces logins but not admin overhead mainly.
Right: lowers admin cost, logs actions.
Metadirectory consolidates data, not cost focused.

questions.stem: During which of the following processes is least privilege implemented for a user account?
questions.explanation: Least privilege is put into effect when the account is actually provisioned, because that is when specific rights are granted. Request and approval only decide what should be granted, and review checks it afterwards.
optionNotes: Correct: provisioning is when the rights are actually assigned, so least privilege is applied here.
Approval authorizes the request but does not configure any rights.
The request states the need; nothing is granted yet.
Review checks existing access after the fact (detective); it does not implement anything.

questions.stem: Which of the following provides the minimum set of privileges required to perform a job function and restricts the user to a domain with the required privileges?
questions.explanation: Role-based access control gives each role only the privileges its job function needs. A user is limited to the domain of their assigned role, which supports least privilege.
optionNotes: Rule-based access applies global rules regardless of job function.
Correct: RBAC ties a minimal privilege set to the job role.
System-determined access (MAC) is driven by labels, not job function.
Sensitivity-based access is MAC classification, not job-based minimal privilege.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the PRIMARY security concern associated with the implementation of smart cards?
options: Mobile code can be embedded in the card
questions.explanation: Smart cards are physical tokens, so the main operational risk is users losing or misplacing them, which leads to unauthorized use or denied access. The other issues are design limits, not primary security concerns.
optionNotes: Limited memory is a capacity constraint, not a security concern.
Vendor compatibility is an interoperability issue.
Correct: lost or misplaced cards are the main security risk.
Card applets are tightly controlled; embedded mobile code is not the primary concern.

questions.stem: Which of the following questions can be answered using user and group entitlement reporting?
options: When a particular file was last accessed by a user
Change control activities for a particular group of users
The number of failed login attempts for a particular user
Where does a particular user have access within the network
questions.explanation: Entitlement reports list the permissions granted to users and groups, showing where each user has access. They do not record activity events.
optionNotes: Last-access time comes from audit logs, not entitlements.
Change control activity is tracked in change records.
Failed logins are authentication log events.
Correct: entitlement reporting shows where a user has access.

questions.stem: A global organization wants to implement hardware tokens as part of a multifactor authentication solution for remote access. The PRIMARY advantage of this implementation is
questions.explanation: A hardware token adds a possession factor, which makes it much harder for an attacker with stolen passwords to get in. The main benefit is preventing unauthorized remote access.
optionNotes: Enrolling tokens globally is actually harder to scale.
Accountability improves somewhat, but that is secondary.
Correct: MFA protects against unauthorized access.
Tokens add administrative work rather than simplifying it.

questions.stem: Which of the following is BEST suited for exchanging authentication and authorization messages in a multi-party decentralized environment?
questions.explanation: SAML exchanges authentication and authorization assertions between independent parties such as IdPs and SPs. That makes it the standard for decentralized, federated environments.
optionNotes: LDAP is a directory access protocol, not a cross-party assertion exchange.
Correct: SAML carries authN/authZ assertions across parties.
IMAP retrieves mail.
TLS secures the channel but carries no assertions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most helpful in applying the principle of LEAST privilege?
options: Setting up a Virtual Private Network (VPN) tunnel
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said C] Least privilege means a subject can do only what it needs. Sandboxing enforces this directly by limiting a process to the specific memory and resources it requires, and the OSG describes it as applying least privilege to processes. Monitoring privileged sessions is a detective control that reviews how privileges are used. It does not by itself restrict privilege, and job rotation tends to cause privilege creep.
optionNotes: Correct: sandboxing limits a process to only the resources it needs, which directly applies least privilege.
Wrong: a VPN protects data in transit and does not limit what a user or process may do.
Wrong: monitoring privileged sessions is detective. It reviews privilege use but does not restrict privilege.
Wrong: job rotation targets fraud and collusion and can cause privilege creep instead of reducing privilege.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST represents the concept of least privilege?
options: Access to an object is denied unless access is specifically allowed.
Access to an object is only available to the owner.
Access to an object is allowed unless it is protected by the information security policy.
Access to an object is only allowed to authenticated users via an Access Control List (ACL).
questions.explanation: Of these options, default deny with explicit allow comes closest to least privilege, because subjects get only the access specifically granted. The other options describe ownership, default-allow or plain ACL use.
optionNotes: Correct: deny unless specifically allowed means only needed access is granted.
Owner-only access is overly restrictive and not the principle.
Default-allow is the opposite of least privilege.
Authentication via an ACL does not limit access to what is needed.

questions.stem: The BEST method to mitigate the risk of a dictionary attack on a system is to
questions.explanation: Dictionary attacks guess common words. Long, complex passphrases are not in dictionaries, which makes such guessing ineffective. Tokens add a factor but do not fix weak passwords.
optionNotes: A token adds a factor but does not reduce password guessability.
Correct: complex passphrases defeat dictionary word lists.
Password history prevents reuse, not guessing.
Encrypting the ACL has nothing to do with password guessing.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST metric to obtain when gaining support for an Identity and Access Management (IAM) solution?
options: Application connection successes resulting in data leakage
Administrative costs for restoring systems after connection failure
Employee system timeouts from implementing wrong limits
Help desk costs required to support password reset requests
questions.explanation: Password reset help-desk costs are a measurable, recurring expense that IAM features like self-service and SSO directly reduce, making a strong business case.
optionNotes: Data leakage from connections is not an IAM metric.
Restoration costs relate to availability, not IAM.
Timeouts from wrong limits are a configuration issue.
Correct: reset costs show clear ROI for IAM.

questions.stem: The organization would like to deploy an authorization mechanism for an Information Technology (IT) infrastructure project with high employee turnover. Which access control mechanism would be preferred?
questions.explanation: RBAC ties permissions to roles, so with high turnover admins only assign or remove users from roles rather than maintaining per-user rights.
optionNotes: ABAC is powerful but more complex to manage.
DAC relies on owners and is hard to manage at scale.
MAC requires labels and clearances.
Correct: RBAC simplifies joiners/leavers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a benefit in implementing an enterprise Identity and Access Management (IAM) solution?
options: Risk associated with orphan accounts is reduced.
Segregation of duties is automatically enforced.
questions.explanation: Centralized IAM ties accounts to lifecycle events, so leavers' accounts are removed and orphaned accounts decrease.
optionNotes: Complexity is not simplified by IAM.
Correct: orphan account risk drops.
SoD must still be designed.
Confidentiality gain is indirect.

questions.stem: Which security access policy contains fixed security attributes that are used by the system to determine a user's access to a file or object?
questions.explanation: MAC uses fixed labels set by the system/administrator that users cannot change to make access decisions.
optionNotes: Correct: MAC uses fixed attributes.
ACLs are a mechanism, typically DAC.
DAC allows owner changes.
Not a standard model.

questions.stem: Which of the following access management procedures would minimize the possibility of an organization's employees retaining access to secure work areas after they change roles?
questions.explanation: Modifying access when someone changes role removes old rights so they don't retain previous work-area access.
optionNotes: Correct: role change triggers modification.
Recertification is periodic, slower to catch it.
Termination applies to leavers.
Provisioning grants new rights.

questions.stem: When network management is outsourced to third parties, which of the following is the MOST effective method of protecting critical data assets?
options: Log all activities associated with sensitive systems
Confirm that confidentiality agreements are signed
questions.explanation: Strong access controls technically limit what outsourced staff can reach, directly protecting the data.
optionNotes: Logging is detective.
Policy links are weak.
NDAs are deterrent only.
Correct: strong access controls.

questions.stem: The core component of Role Based Access Control (RBAC) must be constructed of defined data elements. Which elements are required?
options: Users, permissions, operations, and protected objects
Roles, accounts, permissions, and protected objects
Users, roles, operations, and protected objects
Roles, operations, accounts, and protected objects
questions.explanation: Core RBAC is built from users, roles, operations and protected objects, with permissions formed by pairing operations with objects.
optionNotes: Omits roles, the central RBAC element
Accounts are not a core RBAC element; omits operations
Correct: NIST core RBAC uses users, roles, operations and objects
Omits users and uses accounts instead

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common feature of an Identity as a Service (IDaaS) solution?
options: Terminal Access Controller Access Control System (TACACS) authentication support
questions.explanation: SSO to cloud and on-premises applications is the defining common feature of IDaaS offerings.
optionNotes: Correct: federated SSO is the defining IDaaS feature
Privileged access management is a separate, specialised product
Self-service reset is common but secondary to SSO
TACACS is an on-premises network-device AAA protocol

questions.stem: Which of the following is the GREATEST benefit of implementing a Role Based Access Control (RBAC) system?
options: Integration using Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP)
Integration with the organizations Human Resources (HR) system
questions.explanation: RBAC simplifies provisioning: users get permissions by being assigned to roles rather than one by one.
optionNotes: LDAP integration is possible without RBAC
Form-based registration is unrelated to RBAC
HR integration is a feature, not RBAC's core benefit
Correct: assigning roles greatly simplifies provisioning

questions.stem: Mandatory Access Controls (MAC) are based on:
options: data labels and user access permissions
questions.explanation: MAC compares subject clearances with object classification labels.
optionNotes: Correct: MAC compares object classification labels with subject clearances
Segmentation is a network concept
User permissions belong to the discretionary model
Roles belong to RBAC; encryption is unrelated

questions.stem: Due to system constraints, a group of system administrators must share a high-level access set of credentials. Which of the following would be MOST appropriate to implement?
options: Increased console lockout times for failed logon attempts
A credential check-out process for a per-use basis
questions.explanation: Checking out a shared credential for each use, with accountability tied to the person, restores individual accountability for shared accounts.
optionNotes: Lockout tuning doesn't fix lost accountability
Fewer sharers still means shared accountability
Correct: per-use check-out ties every use to one individual
Logs show the account, not which person used it

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST Identity-as-a-Service (IDaaS) solution for validating users?
questions.explanation: SAML carries authentication assertions between the identity provider and the service, validating users in federated IDaaS.
optionNotes: SSO is an outcome, not a validation standard
Correct: SAML assertions validate user identity across domains
LDAP is a directory protocol, not a cloud federation standard
OAuth is authorization, not authentication

questions.stem: What capability would typically be included in a commercially available software package designed for access control?
questions.explanation: Access control packages store and protect credentials, so protecting (encrypting/hashing) passwords is a typical built-in capability.
optionNotes: Correct: credential protection
Data protection product function
Software configuration management
Not a standard term/feature

questions.stem: Which Identity and Access Management (IAM) process can be used to maintain the principle of least privilege?
questions.explanation: Periodic access reviews detect privilege creep and remove excess rights, maintaining least privilege.
optionNotes: Provisioning grants initial access; it does not trim rights over time
Access recovery restores lost credentials; unrelated to privilege scope
MFA strengthens authentication but does not limit privileges
Correct: periodic reviews remove accumulated excess rights

questions.stem: Which of the following is BEST achieved through the use of eXtensible Access Markup Language (XACML)?
options: Minimize malicious attacks from third parties
Share digital identities in hybrid cloud
questions.explanation: XACML expresses fine-grained authorization policies controlling resource privileges.
optionNotes: XACML does not reduce attacks; it expresses authorization policy
Correct: XACML defines fine-grained policies for resource access
Sharing identities across domains is SAML/federation
XACML is a policy language, and 'a standard protocol' is too vague

questions.stem: An organization's security policy delegates to the data owner the ability to assign which user roles have access to a particular resource. What type of authorization mechanism is being used?
questions.explanation: The owner deciding at their discretion who gets access is discretionary access control.
optionNotes: Correct
Roles are used but assignment at owner discretion defines DAC
Network layer term
System-enforced labels

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST effective practice in managing user accounts when an employee is terminated?
options: Implement processes for automated removal of access for terminated employees.
Delete employee network and system IDs upon termination.
Manually remove terminated employee user-access to all systems and applications.
Disable terminated employee network ID to remove all access.
questions.explanation: Automated deprovisioning ensures timely, complete removal.
optionNotes: Correct: automated deprovisioning is timely and complete across systems
Immediate deletion destroys audit trail and owned data
Manual removal risks missing systems
Disabling only network ID misses local/cloud accounts

questions.stem: A company needs to provide employee access to travel services, which are hosted by a third-party service provider, Employee experience is important, and when users are already authenticated, access to the travel portal is seamless. Which of the following methods is used to share information and grant user access to the travel portal?
questions.explanation: SAML assertions let an IdP pass authentication to a third-party SP, giving seamless federated access. SSO is the resulting experience and federation the trust relationship, but SAML is the actual exchange format.
optionNotes: SAML carries authentication assertions from IdP to the third-party SP, enabling seamless access.
SSO is the user experience outcome, not the information-sharing mechanism.
OAuth is for delegated authorization, not passing authentication to a portal.
Federation is the trust concept; SAML is the method that shares the identity data.

questions.stem: A security professional has been assigned to assess a web application. The assessment report recommends switching to Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML). What is the PRIMARY security benefit in switching to SAML?
options: It uses Transport Layer Security (TLS) to address confidentiality.
It enables single sign-on (SSO) for web applications.
The users' password is not passed during authentication.
It limits unnecessary data entry on web forms.
questions.explanation: With SAML the SP receives a signed assertion; the user's password is never sent to the application. Keeping credentials away from the service provider removes password exposure at the application.
optionNotes: TLS is a transport feature, not a SAML benefit.
SSO is a usability benefit, not the primary security one.
The app receives a signed assertion, never the user's password.
Reduced data entry is convenience, not security.

questions.stem: A project requires the use of an authentication mechanism where playback must be protected and plaintext secret must be used. Which of the following should be used?
questions.explanation: CHAP uses challenge-response with a shared plaintext secret, protecting against replay. The changing challenge means captured responses can't be replayed.
optionNotes: PAP sends cleartext passwords and allows replay.
EAP is a framework, not itself a mechanism.
SHA is a hash, not an authentication protocol.
CHAP challenge-response uses a plaintext shared secret and resists replay.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST secure password technique?
questions.explanation: OTPs are valid only once, defeating replay and reuse. Even if intercepted, an OTP is useless afterward.
optionNotes: Passphrases are reusable and can be stolen.
OTPs are valid once, defeating replay.
Cognitive passwords are guessable from public facts.
Ciphertext is not a password technique.

questions.stem: A large organization's human resources and security teams are planning on implementing technology to eliminate manual user access reviews and improve compliance. Which of the following options is MOST likely to resolve the issues associated with user access?
options: Implement a role-based access control (RBAC) system.
Implement identity and access management (IAM) platform.
Implement a Privileged Access Management (PAM) system.
questions.explanation: An IAM platform automates provisioning, reviews and certification. Automated certification campaigns replace manual reviews and give compliance evidence.
optionNotes: RBAC is a model; it doesn't automate reviews itself.
An IAM platform automates provisioning and access certification.
PAM covers only privileged accounts.
SSO improves login, not access reviews.

questions.stem: When should an application invoke re-authentication in addition to initial user authentication?
questions.explanation: Re-authentication after inactivity limits session hijacking of idle sessions. It counters someone using an unattended logged-in session.
optionNotes: Sign-off ends the session.
Periodic re-auth hurts usability without a trigger.
Inactivity re-auth protects unattended sessions.
Per-process re-auth is excessive.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes centralized identity management?
options: Service providers rely on a trusted third party (TTP) to provide requestors with both credentials and identifiers.
Service providers agree to integrate identity system recognition across organizational boundaries.
Service providers identify an entity by behavior analysis versus an identification factor.
Service providers perform as both the credential and identity provider (IdP).
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said D] Identity management models include isolated, centralized and federated. In the centralized model, one trusted entity issues both the credentials and the identifiers, and every service provider relies on it. When each service provider issues its own credentials and identifiers, that is the isolated model. When providers agree to recognize each other's identities across organizations, that is federation.
optionNotes: Correct: one trusted third party supplies credentials and identifiers that all service providers rely on, which is centralized IdM.
Wrong: integrating identity recognition across organizational boundaries describes federated identity.
Wrong: behavior analysis is a behavioral biometric or analytics technique, not an IdM model.
Wrong: each service provider acting as its own credential and identity provider is the isolated model.

questions.stem: In a large company, a system administrator needs to assign users access to files using Role Based Access Control (RBAC). Which option is an example of RBAC?
options: Allowing users access to files based on their group membership
Allowing users access to files based on username
Allowing users access to files based on the users location at time of access
Allowing users access to files based on the file type
questions.explanation: RBAC grants permissions to roles or groups that reflect job functions, and users inherit access through membership. Granting access based on group membership is the example that matches.
optionNotes: Right: access through group/role membership is RBAC.
Per-username permissions are discretionary/identity-based, not role-based.
Location-based conditions are attribute- or rule-based controls.
File-type based access is an attribute of the object, not a role.

questions.stem: After a breach incident, investigators narrowed the attack to a specific network administrator's credentials. However, there was no evidence to determine how the hackers obtained the credentials. Which of the following actions could have BEST avoided the above breach per the investigation described above?
options: A periodic review of network access logs
A periodic review of active users on the network
A periodic review of all privileged accounts actions
A periodic review of password strength of all users across the organization
questions.explanation: The administrator's privileged credentials were misused, so regularly reviewing what privileged accounts actually do would have spotted the abnormal activity early. Privileged account monitoring is the key control for admin credential abuse.
optionNotes: General access-log review is broader and less focused on admin misuse.
Listing active users won't show misuse of valid admin credentials.
Right: reviewing privileged account actions detects misuse of admin credentials.
Password strength doesn't address how the credentials were obtained or misused.

questions.stem: Which of the following presents the PRIMARY concern to an organization when setting up a federated single sign-on (SSO) solution with another organization?
options: Sending assertions to an identity provider
Requesting Identity assertions from the partners domain
Having the resource provider query the Identity provider
questions.explanation: In federation, each party's identities and attributes must be mapped to the other side's accounts and privileges. Defining that mapping scheme is the main design concern; sending and requesting assertions is just how the protocol works.
optionNotes: Assertions are sent from the IdP, not to it; this is protocol mechanics.
Requesting assertions is a normal SSO flow step.
Right: identity mapping between domains is the main federation concern.
The relying party querying the IdP is normal protocol behaviour.

questions.stem: A user is allowed to access the file labeled "Financial Forecast," but only between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. Which type of access mechanism should be used to accomplish this?
questions.explanation: Time-of-day restrictions are global rules applied to access attempts, which is rule-based access control. ACLs and RBAC alone don't express time windows natively.
optionNotes: 'Minimum access control' isn't a standard model.
Right: time-based restrictions are rule-based access control.
Roles don't inherently restrict by time.
ACLs list subjects and permissions, not time conditions.

questions.stem: A client server infrastructure that provides user-to-server authentication describes which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Kerberos is a client-server authentication protocol in which a trusted KDC issues tickets that authenticate users to servers. SSL/TLS typically authenticates the server to the client.
optionNotes: SSL/TLS mainly authenticates servers to clients.
Right: Kerberos provides user-to-server authentication.
X.509 is a certificate format, not an authentication infrastructure.
Authorization is not authentication.

questions.stem: What is the MOST significant benefit of role-based access control (RBAC)?
options: Most granular form of access control
questions.explanation: RBAC assigns permissions to roles rather than to individuals, which greatly reduces the effort of granting and revoking access as people join, move or leave. Lower administrative overhead is its main benefit.
optionNotes: Right: role-level administration reduces overhead.
Reduced inappropriate access is a by-product, not the main benefit.
RBAC can support least privilege, but so can other models.
ABAC is more granular than RBAC.

questions.stem: Which of the following authorization standards is built to handle Application Programming Interface (API) access for Federated Identity Management (FIM)?
options: Terminal Access Control Access Control System Plus (TACACS+)
questions.explanation: OAuth is an authorization framework designed to delegate API access across federated parties. SAML is aimed at browser SSO assertions, while RADIUS and TACACS+ are network/device AAA protocols.
optionNotes: Mainly authentication/SSO assertions for browsers
Correct: delegated API authorization
Network access AAA protocol
Device administration AAA

questions.stem: After the INITIAL input of a user identification (ID) and password, what is an authentication system that prompts the user for a different response each time the user logs on?
questions.explanation: Challenge-response systems present a different challenge each logon, requiring a different response. PINs and secondary passwords stay the same between logons, and voice is a biometric trait rather than a changing response.
optionNotes: Static secret that is reused
Static secret that is reused
Correct: a new challenge needs a new answer
Biometric trait that does not change per session

questions.stem: When using Security Assertion markup language (SAML), it is assumed that the principal subject
options: accepts persistent cookies from the system.
allows Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) for data exchanges.
is on a system that supports remote authorization.
enrolls with at least one identity provider.
questions.explanation: SAML assumes the principal has enrolled with at least one identity provider that asserts its identity. Trust in SAML flows from the IdP to the service provider, so the subject must have an account at an IdP.
optionNotes: Not assumed
Transport detail
Not assumed
Correct

questions.stem: Which of the following is the FIRST step during digital identity provisioning?
options: Authorizing the entity for resource access
Creating the entity record with the correct attributes
questions.explanation: Provisioning starts by creating the identity record with correct attributes; authorization and credentials follow. An entity must exist with accurate attributes before it can receive credentials, synchronization or authorizations.
optionNotes: Authorization needs an existing identity first
Synchronization happens after the record exists
Credentials are issued to an existing record
Correct: the identity record comes first

questions.stem: Which of the following is a process in the access provisioning lifecycle that will MOST likely identify access aggregation issues?
questions.explanation: Periodic access reviews detect privilege accumulation/aggregation. Reviews compare accumulated rights against the current job role, which reveals privilege creep and toxic combinations.
optionNotes: Testing is not a provisioning lifecycle step
Too general
Correct: periodic access review finds privilege creep
Code review practice

questions.stem: Which of the following is the MOST significant benefit to implementing a third-party federated identity architecture?
options: Attribute assertions as agencies can request a larger set of attributes to fulfill service delivery
Data decrease related to storing personal information
Reduction in operational costs to the agency
Enable business objectives so departments can focus on mission rather than the business of identity management
questions.explanation: Third-party federation lets the organization focus on its mission rather than running identity management. Cost and data reduction are side benefits, but the strategic benefit is enabling the business.
optionNotes: Over-collecting attributes is a privacy risk, not a benefit
Side benefit
Side benefit
Correct: focus on mission

questions.stem: In order to support the least privilege security principle when a resource is transferring within the organization from a production support system administration role to a developer role, what changes should be made to the resource's access to the production operating system (OS) directory structure?
options: From Read Only privileges to No Access Privileges
From Author privileges to Administrator privileges
From Administrator privileges to No Access privileges
From No Access Privileges to Author privileges
questions.explanation: A developer should have no access to production; prior admin rights must be removed. Developers should not keep production access, because it violates least privilege and separation of duties.
optionNotes: Admins did not have read-only access
Increases privilege
Correct: remove all production access
Grants unnecessary access

questions.stem: An organization has implemented a protection strategy to secure the network from unauthorized external access. The new Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) wants to increase security by better protecting the network from unauthorized internal access. Which Network Access Control (NAC) capability BEST meets this objective?
questions.explanation: Network Access Control decides which devices may connect to internal network ports. Port security (for example 802.1X, or MAC limits on switch ports) blocks rogue internal devices at the point of connection, which matches the CISO's goal of stopping unauthorized internal access.
optionNotes: An application firewall filters application-layer traffic; it does not gate device access to the LAN
Right: a port-level NAC control against internal rogue connections
Password strength is an authentication policy, not a NAC capability
2FA strengthens user login but does not stop an unauthorized device from plugging in

questions.stem: An organization has implemented a password complexity and an account lockout policy enforcing five incorrect logins tries within ten minutes. Network users have reported significantly increased account lockouts. Which of the following security principles is this company affecting?
questions.explanation: Aggressive lockout thresholds lock out legitimate users who mistype complex passwords. The resulting denial of access to resources is an availability impact.
optionNotes: Right: users are denied access, which is an availability impact
Data integrity is not affected by lockouts
Lockouts protect confidentiality rather than harm it
Authentication is a security service, not one of the CIA principles

questions.stem: Which access control method is based on users issuing access requests on system resources, features assigned to those resources, the operational or situational context, and a set of policies specified in terms of those features and context?
questions.explanation: NIST SP 800-162 defines ABAC as granting access based on attributes of the subject, the object and the environment or context, evaluated against policy. The stem paraphrases that definition.
optionNotes: MAC compares security labels and clearances
RBAC grants access by job role
DAC lets the owner grant access at their discretion
Right: attributes plus context evaluated against policy is ABAC

questions.stem: Which of the following is an open standard for exchanging authentication and authorization data between parties?
questions.explanation: SAML is the OASIS XML-based open standard for exchanging authentication and authorization assertions between an identity provider and a service provider. It underpins much web single sign-on.
optionNotes: 'Wired markup language' is a distractor (WML is the Wireless Markup Language)
HTML structures web pages and carries no assertions
XML is the generic syntax SAML is built on, not the exchange standard itself
Right: SAML exchanges authentication and authorization data

questions.stem: Which of the following factors should be considered characteristics of Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) in terms of the attributes used?
options: Mandatory Access Control (MAC) and Discretionary Access Control (DAC)
Discretionary Access Control (DAC) and Access Control List (ACL)
Role Based Access Control (RBAC) and Mandatory Access Control (MAC)
Role Based Access Control (RBAC) and Access Control List (ACL)
questions.explanation: ABAC policies can use role information (like RBAC) as one subject attribute and express resource permissions in an ACL-like way. RBAC and ACL concepts are therefore the characteristics that ABAC attributes can include.
optionNotes: MAC labels and DAC owner discretion are not presented as ABAC's attribute characteristics
DAC is ownership-based, not attribute-based
MAC is label- and clearance-based
Right: role attributes and ACL-style resource rules

questions.stem: An organization wants a service provider to authenticate users via the users' organization domain credentials. Which markup language should the organization's security personnel use to support the integration?
questions.explanation: SAML carries federated authentication assertions from IdP to service provider. The organization acts as the identity provider and the vendor as the service provider.
optionNotes: SAML exchanges authentication assertions between an IdP and an SP.
A data serialization format, not a federation standard.
A web page markup language.
Generic markup; SAML is built on it, but XML alone does not federate.

questions.stem: The security team plans on using automated account reconciliation in the corporate user access review process. Which of the following must be implemented for the BEST results with fewest errors when running the audit?
options: Removal of service accounts from review
questions.explanation: Automated reconciliation compares accounts against clear provisioning rules; without them, errors abound. Without clear rules, the tool flags false mismatches.
optionNotes: Service accounts still need review.
SoD is a separate control objective.
Clear provisioning rules give reconciliation a baseline to compare against.
Audit frequency does not reduce reconciliation errors.

questions.stem: When developing the entitlement review process, which of the following roles is responsible for determining who has a need for the information?
questions.explanation: The data owner decides who needs access. Owners approve entitlements in reviews.
optionNotes: Custodians implement controls; they do not decide need.
The owner determines who needs access.
A DBA is a custodian role.
Not the accountable role for data access.

questions.stem: Which open standard could a large corporation deploy for authorization services for single sign-on (SSO) use across multiple internal and external application?
options: Terminal Access Controller Access Control System (TACACS)
questions.explanation: SAML is an open standard for cross-domain SSO assertions. It works across internal and external apps.
optionNotes: An AAA protocol for device administration.
SAML is the open federated SSO standard.
A directory protocol, not cross-domain SSO.
A Microsoft product, not an open standard.

questions.stem: Which of the following terms BEST describes a system which allows a user to log in and access multiple related servers and applications?
questions.explanation: Single sign-on allows one authentication to access multiple related systems within an organization.
optionNotes: RDP is remote access
FIM spans organizations; SSO best fits related internal servers
Right: Single sign-on allows one authentication to access multiple related systems within an organization.
MFA concerns factors

questions.stem: A company is attempting to enhance the security of its user authentication processes. After evaluating several options, the company has decided to utilize Identity as a Service (IDaaS). Which of the following factors leads the company to choose an IDaaS as their solution?
options: In-house team lacks resources to support an on-premise solution.
Third-party solutions are inherently more secure.
Third-party solutions are known for transferring the risk to the vendor.
questions.explanation: IDaaS is typically selected when internal staff lack the resources to build and operate an on-premises identity solution.
optionNotes: In-house is the opposite of IDaaS
Right: IDaaS is typically selected when internal staff lack the resources to build and operate an on-premises identity solution.
Third parties are not inherently more secure
Risk ownership is not transferred

questions.stem: In Identity Management (IdM), when is the verification stage performed?
questions.explanation: Identity proofing/verification occurs before the identity is created and provisioned.
optionNotes: Sign-on is authentication
Right: Identity proofing/verification occurs before the identity is created and provisioned.
Revocation ends lifecycle
Authorization follows

questions.stem: A company developed a web application which is sold as a Software as a Service (SaaS) solution to the customer. The application is hosted by a web server running on a specific operating system (OS) on a virtual machine (VM). During the transition phase of the service, it is determined that the support team will need access to the application logs. Which of the following privileges would be the MOST suitable?
options: Administrative privileges on the web server
Administrative privileges on the application folders
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said B] Least privilege says the support team should get only what is needed to read logs, i.e., access to the application folders where logs are kept. Admin rights on the web server, OS or hypervisor grant far more control than the task requires.
optionNotes: OS admin is far broader than log access.
Web server admin allows reconfiguring the service; excessive.
Hypervisor admin would expose all VMs; grossly excessive.
Correct: scoped access to application/log folders meets the need with least privilege.

questions.stem: Which type of access control includes a system that allows only users that are type=managers and department=sales to access employee records?
questions.explanation: [Key corrected: book said C] Decisions based on combinations of user attributes such as type=manager and department=sales are attribute-based access control. RBAC would grant by a single assigned role, not by evaluating multiple attributes.
optionNotes: DAC is owner-discretion, not attribute rules.
MAC uses classification labels and clearances.
RBAC grants by role membership, not attribute policy expressions.
Correct: policy evaluates multiple subject attributes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a characteristic of a challenge/response authentication process?
